title: Technical Guidance: Phishing and Smishing Structural Indicators
source: ScamShield AI Research Taxonomy & Industry Best Practice
content:
Phishing and SMS phishing (smishing) rely on cognitive manipulation combined with technical obfuscation techniques to deceive recipients into surrendering sensitive information or executing unauthorized actions.

1. Structural URL Risk Indicators:
Phishing links frequently exhibit distinct technical anomalies:
- IP-based hostnames (e.g., http://192.168.1.1/login) used to avoid domain reputation tracking.
- Subdomain typosquatting or brand spoofing (e.g., sbi.banking-portal.com or hdfc-secure-auth.top).
- Excessive URL shortening or redirection chains to mask destination servers.
- Inclusion of sensitive keywords in path elements (e.g., /verify, /login, /unlock, /kyc-update) combined with newly registered generic top-level domains (.xyz, .top, .online, .site).
- Embedded userinfo elements (e.g., https://legit-bank.com@evil-site.com) designed to deceive visual inspection.

2. Behavioral & Tactical Pressure Patterns:
Phishing communications predominantly deploy artificial urgency, fear of financial loss, or excessive reward incentives. Common manifestations include:
- Imposing severe time constraints (e.g., 'within 30 minutes', 'before 11:59 PM tonight').
- Threatening severe punitive action (e.g., 'permanent forfeiture of funds', 'legal arrest warrant issued', 'SIM card deactivation').
- Demanding non-standard communication channels (e.g., insisting on contacting a personal WhatsApp number or non-toll-free mobile number).
